name: runtime-data-boundary-registry
purpose: Defines how the platform separates repository source code, installed product code, user workspaces, accumulated data stores, logs, and agent work areas so the development repository can build the platform while end users receive an installable app without platform source visibility.

reader_guide.summary: Use this registry before adding product storage, log capture, agent workspaces, installer payloads, or customer-facing workspace features. It is the steering contract for code/data/log/agent boundaries.
how_to_read: Read customer_visibility_policy first to understand what an installed user should and should not see.
Read repository_planes to know what remains in this development repository.
Read installed_product_planes to know what the shipped app owns at runtime.
Read runtime_data_roots and log_taxonomy before adding data accumulation or log persistence.
Read agent_workspace_policy before creating or moving agent definitions, agent runtime state, or task work folders.
update_triggers: The desktop app adds a new persisted data store, log stream, agent runtime state, or workspace artifact.
The installer payload, app bundle resources, source map policy, or customer-visible file layout changes.
A new local service, sidecar, worker, or CLI adapter needs persistent state.
User workspace import/export, backup, migration, or retention behavior changes.
Agent definitions or agent task execution folders are reorganized.

structure_rules.rule: This repository may contain platform source, product specifications, developer fixtures, and generated monitor snapshots, but public installers must not expose the repository source tree as the customer workspace.
structure_rules.reason: The user wants this repo to build the platform while installed customers use the product without seeing platform source code.

structure_rules.rule: User data stores, task artifacts, logs, accumulated evidence, and agent runtime state are runtime data planes, not platform source code.
structure_rules.reason: The platform must keep building logic separate from accumulated customer data and operational logs.

structure_rules.rule: Logs must be classified by operational purpose before retention, migration, export, or model consumption.
structure_rules.reason: Raw logs can contain sensitive user data, secrets, or low-value noise; durable accumulation needs provenance, redaction, and retention rules.

structure_rules.rule: Reusable agent definitions stay in agent registries; agent runtime task work should be grouped in an agent workspace plane with scoped inputs, outputs, logs, and cleanup.
structure_rules.reason: Agents need a common place to work without scattering runtime state through product source folders.

structure_rules.rule: The installed shell must read the bundled installer shell runtime contract before task execution, write task, decision, evidence, validation, and evaluation records to the declared data accumulation targets, and expose a user-visible accumulated data index backed by a versioned manifest.
structure_rules.reason: The desktop product exists to turn repository knowledge into enforced runtime behavior and accumulated operating data.

field_guide.meaning: Defines what installed customers can see, configure, export, or inspect, and what platform source remains hidden from the customer product surface.
Development-repository planes that contain source, specs, configs, docs, tests, templates, and local-only scratch.
Runtime planes in the installed app: app bundle, user workspace, user data store, logs, agent workspace, cache, and export/import surfaces.
Preferred platform-neutral runtime storage roots and their OS-specific direction.
Log classes, examples, retention posture, privacy controls, and product visibility.
Rules for where agent definitions, generated agent work, task artifacts, and agent logs belong.

customer_visibility_policy.policy: Installed customers use the app, selected user workspaces, exported reports, and configurable data/log locations. They do not receive the platform development repository, source tree, internal specs, private history, or developer-only generated snapshots as a product feature.
customer_visible: workspace chooser and customer-selected workspace paths
customer-visible audit/log summaries after redaction and retention filtering
customer_hidden: source maps unless explicitly required for support builds
agent implementation source not needed for customer configuration
customer_visibility_policy.support_exception: A support or enterprise diagnostic bundle may expose bounded metadata and redacted logs only through an explicit export action, retention policy, and privacy review.

repository_planes.label: Platform Source
repository_planes.purpose: Developer-owned source, config, tests, validators, and product logic used to build the platform.

repository_planes.label: Developer Governance
repository_planes.purpose: Durable repository knowledge, planning, requirements, validation, and history for platform development.

repository_planes.label: Developer Artifacts
repository_planes.purpose: Build-time or developer-visible artifacts. Public deployment requires privacy review before exposing generated snapshots.

repository_planes.label: Local Only Private
repository_planes.purpose: Ignored local scratch, sensitive files, and transient tool output.

installed_product_planes.label: Installed App Bundle
contents: signed helper binaries when explicitly approved

installed_product_planes.label: User Workspace
contents: repositories cloned through the desktop Workspace Host

runtime_data_roots.macos_direction: Use app container, Application Support, app group container, or user-selected workspace paths according to signing and sandbox level.
runtime_data_roots.windows_direction: Use LocalAppData/Roaming app data stores according to update, roaming, and privacy behavior.
runtime_data_roots.tauri_direction: Prefer Tauri app-specific base directories and permission-scoped filesystem access before custom absolute paths.
runtime_data_roots.repository_development_direction: During local development, project artifacts may exist under platform-desktop-app/artifacts/ only when ignored or explicitly tracked as durable fixtures.

log_taxonomy.label: Task Execution
privacy_controls: redact sensitive paths before support export

agent_workspace_policy.repository_fixture_home: agent-platform/artifacts/ or platform-desktop-app/artifacts/ only for durable fixtures or ignored local output
rules: Reusable agent definitions, tools, metadata, triggers, and validation handles belong in agent-platform/configs/agents/.
Agent docs belong in agent-platform/docs/ unless the agent is project-specific and registered in the owning project.
Installed runtime task work must not be scattered through source folders; it belongs in the agent workspace plane with task IDs, lane IDs, input/output/log separation, and cleanup policy.
Agent logs must use log_taxonomy before retention or support export.
Agent runtime work may read or write customer-selected workspaces only through permission-scoped commands and path allowlists.

privacy_controls: Do not bundle _private, outputs, unredacted logs, secrets, browser cookies, or private snapshots.
Do not expose platform source code to customers as an installed app feature.
Use source maps only in explicitly approved internal or support builds.
Classify and redact logs before model ingestion, support export, or public snapshot generation.
Keep client-side hiding separate from server/collector-side data exclusion.

allowed: static frontend assets required by the app
signed helper binaries or sidecars after audit
disallowed: _history and internal specs as product-visible files
real secrets, tokens, cookies, private snapshots

implementation_sequence.description: Keep this registry and product boundary docs updated before implementing new runtime stores.
Define schemas for task records, logs, agent work packets, and settings before writing runtime files.
Implement OS-aware app data/log/cache directories with permission-scoped paths.
Add retention, redaction, support export, and customer-visible inspection flows.

Expose a bounded read-only index of accumulated task runs, decisions, audits, support bundles, and agent work, and persist it as app_data/runtime-data/indexes/accumulated-data-overview.v1.json so users can inspect what the product is storing.
Persist app-owned workspace state and expose existing-workspace import plus bounded Git clone so users do not need to manually clone and run tools from a development repository.
Run installer payload audit to confirm platform source and private data are not exposed.
